backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/delay.rs:53-60 (DelayConfig::to_duration) multiplies the user-supplied `duration: u64` field (declared at delay.rs:44) by the unit factor with a plain `*`: `Duration::from_secs(self.duration * 60)` (Minutes), `* 3600` (Hours), `* 86400` (Days). None of these multiplications is checked or saturating.

The multiply runs BEFORE the range validation. DelayExecutor::execute calls `let duration = delay_config.to_duration();` at delay.rs:100 and only THEN checks `if duration.as_secs() > MAX_DELAY_SECONDS` at delay.rs:103 (MAX_DELAY_SECONDS = 7 days, delay.rs:65). So the overflow happens inside to_duration() — the 7-day cap can never guard the arithmetic that precedes it.

Reachability: workflow action `config` is arbitrary serde_json deserialized straight into DelayConfig (parse_config at delay.rs:78-80, no bound on `duration`). A workflow-action definition with e.g. `{"duration": 9223372036854775807, "unit": "days"}` makes `self.duration * 86400` overflow u64. In debug / overflow-checks builds (the profile CI runs `cargo test` under) this PANICS, killing the workflow-executor task that drives the delay step (DoS of the action pipeline); in release it silently wraps to an arbitrary small value that then passes the MAX_DELAY_SECONDS check — a validation bypass rather than the intended ConfigurationError rejection.

This is an oversight, not a house convention: the sibling backoff helper in the SAME crate was explicitly hardened against exactly this class of bug — backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:35-46 (compute_backoff_seconds) caps the exponent and uses `base.saturating_mul(multiplier)` with a doc comment citing the overflow audit. Landable backend-only fix: use `checked_mul`/`saturating_mul` in to_duration() (returning a ConfigurationError on overflow), or validate `self.duration` magnitude in parse_config before the unit multiply, so an out-of-range delay is rejected as a config error instead of panicking or wrapping past the 7-day cap.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/document_generation.rs:536-540 collapses a missing LLM completion to an empty string: `let content = response.choices.first().map(|c| c.message.content.clone()).unwrap_or_default();`. When the provider returns 200 with an empty `choices` array (content-filter block, provider hiccup, quota/streaming truncation), `content` becomes "" and the branch is indistinguishable from a genuine empty answer.

The empty string is then fed to parse_summary_response("") (document_generation.rs:558) which yields an empty summary and no key points, and the method still returns `Ok(DocumentSummarizationResult { summary: "", key_points: [], word_count: 0, tokens_used: response.usage.total_tokens, .. })` (document_generation.rs:547-554). The caller receives a SUCCESS carrying an empty document summary rather than an error it can retry or surface.

The same pattern repeats for announcement drafting at document_generation.rs:706-711 (`.unwrap_or_default()` on `choices.first()`), where parse_announcement_drafts("") (document_generation.rs:799) returns an empty Vec and the call still succeeds with zero drafts — a silent no-op generation.

Landable backend-only fix: when `response.choices` is empty, return a domain error (e.g. a new `DocumentGenerationError::EmptyCompletion` / the crate's existing LLM error variant) instead of `unwrap_or_default()`, so an empty/blocked upstream response is reported as a failure rather than a successful-but-empty summary/announcement. Unit-testable with a stubbed LLM client returning `choices: []`.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/api/DecimalStringSerializers.kt:44-47 and :60-63 — the wire-tolerant monetary deserializers finish by calling `raw.substringBefore('.').toLong()` (DecimalAsLongSerializer) and `raw.toDouble()` (DecimalAsDoubleSerializer) directly on the raw JSON primitive content. Both `String.toLong()` and `String.toDouble()` throw NumberFormatException on any content that is not a clean numeric literal: an empty string "", a thousands-separated value like "1,000.00", a leading-'+' value, whitespace, scientific notation, or any non-numeric string the backend might emit.

This defeats the exact purpose the serializers were introduced for. Their own doc comment (:12-32) says they exist because a fractional `serde-str` value like "200000.00" against a bare Long "silently killed the whole price-tracking payload decode (see issue #2331)". But an unexpected/malformed value now throws inside the serializer, which aborts the ENTIRE object decode — so a single bad monetary field still fails the whole favorites/price-tracking payload (`GET /api/v1/favorites`, `GET /api/v1/favorites/alerts`), reproducing the same all-or-nothing failure mode #2331 was meant to eliminate. The FavoritesRepository catch(e: Exception) (FavoritesRepository.kt:39,162) downgrades it to a failed Result rather than an app crash, so the user sees the whole Price-Tracking screen error out on one malformed field instead of a graceful per-field fallback.

Test gap confirming the exposure: DecimalWireContractTest.kt (the stated CI guard for these serializers, issue #2364) only pins happy-path shapes — fractional string, plain number, and JSON null (:44-152). There is NO test for empty-string, non-numeric, or otherwise malformed content, so this brittleness is unguarded. Fix: parse defensively — e.g. `raw.substringBefore('.').toLongOrNull() ?: 0L` and `raw.toDoubleOrNull() ?: 0.0` (or a documented sentinel), and add malformed-input cases to DecimalWireContractTest so the tolerance contract is actually enforced. Static-analysis finding: the throwing call is clear from source; runtime frequency depends on backend output.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:33-40 — eventToQueryKeys subscribes to COLON-form event names ('entity:announcement','entity:fault','entity:vote','entity:document','entity:message','entity:neighbor'), and :313 subscribes to generic 'entity:updated'/'entity:created'/'entity:deleted'. These are the ONLY keys wired for TanStack Query cache invalidation on server push.

The server publishes DOT-form event names. Confirmed in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ws_notifications.rs:92-95 (WsEvent.event mirrors PubSubMessage::event_type, e.g. 'notification.created','preference.updated') and backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification_pipeline.rs:169 (`let event_type = format!("{}.notification", entity_type)` → 'announcements.notification','fault.notification', etc.). Other confirmed literals: 'fault.created','vote.closed'.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:65-82 parseServerMessage maps the server envelope's `event` string straight onto `message.type` with NO dot→colon normalization, and WebSocketService.subscribe (websocket.ts:466) keys handlers off that raw `message.type`. Grep confirms there is no remapping layer anywhere in lib/hooks/contexts and no subscriber uses the dot-form names.

Net effect: the colon-form subscription keys can NEVER match the dot-form event names the server actually emits, so WebSocket-driven query invalidation is entirely dead — real-time announcements/faults/votes/documents pushes never invalidate any cache and the UI shows stale data until a manual refetch/navigation. Traced both ends (server publish site → client subscribe keys), no overlap → high confidence.

Fix: align the client subscription keys with the server's dot-form event_type namespace (e.g. map 'announcements.notification'/'fault.created'/'vote.closed'/'*.notification' → the right query keys), or normalize server event names to the colon scheme in parseServerMessage. Add a test asserting an emitted 'fault.created' frame invalidates the ['faults'] query.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:337 — AuthProvider wires the hand-rolled axios client via `configureApiClient({ getToken: getAccessToken })`, passing ONLY getToken and never an `onUnauthorized` callback.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:195-196,219-220 — createAxiosInstance stores `onUnauthorizedCallback = config.onUnauthorized` (module global) and the response interceptor only reacts to a 401 when `onUnauthorizedCallback` is truthy: `if (error.response?.status === 401 && onUnauthorizedCallback) onUnauthorizedCallback();`. Because AuthContext never supplies it, the callback is permanently undefined and the entire 401 branch is dead for this client.

This client is NOT unused: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts:19 and frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:10 both document their reliance on it ('401 → onUnauthorized') — an expectation the wiring silently breaks.

Net effect: when a feature hook using getApiClient() hits a 401 (access token expired mid-session), there is no silent token refresh, no logout, and no redirect-to-login — the user just gets a failed request and a stuck/dead session until they manually reload. The AuthProvider already owns a refreshToken() routine that could be wired here.
Fix: pass `onUnauthorized` into configureApiClient (e.g. attempt refreshToken(); on failure call logout()), matching the documented contract in the sentiment/predictive-maintenance hooks.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:220-233 decodeJwtPayload does an UNVERIFIED base64 decode of the JWT payload (no signature check — the browser has no verifying key), and :254-258 deriveActiveRole trusts the embedded `claims.role` string: `if (claims.role is string && ROLE_PRIORITY.includes(claimRole)) return claimRole` — this becomes the user's effective role.

That derived role is persisted and set into React state (AuthContext.tsx:387-389 in refreshTokenInternal, and :477-479/:513-516 in login/loginWithSsoCode), so any UI role-gating that reads user.role trusts a value taken from an unverified, client-mutable token (localStorage key 'ppt_access_token').

Impact is bounded — the api-server still enforces real authorization server-side, so this cannot bypass backend checks; the risk is purely UI-level (a user who edits their stored token could reveal admin-only UI affordances / menu items). Low severity, but it is a genuine 'trust unverified JWT claim' smell in the auth core.

Fix: treat the client-derived role as advisory only and ensure every privileged UI surface is also guarded by a server-authoritative capability/permission check (or a role echoed by a signed server response) rather than the decoded token claim; add a comment documenting that decodeJwtPayload is unverified and UI-only.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/components/MediationChatThread.tsx:28 — `const { data: notes = [], isLoading } = useMediationNotes(disputeId);` drops isError; a failed notes fetch resolves isLoading=false with notes=[] and renders the 'disputes.mediation.noMessages' empty state (line 69-73), indistinguishable from a genuinely empty thread and with no retry affordance.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/components/MediationTimelineView.tsx:51 — `const { data: events, isLoading } = useDisputeTimeline(disputeId);` drops isError; on fetch failure `events` is undefined so the `if (!events || events.length === 0)` branch (line 60) shows 'disputes.mediation.noTimelineEvents' instead of an error/retry.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/components/MediationSubmissionsPanel.tsx:43 — `const { data: submissions = [], isLoading } = useDisputeSubmissions(disputeId);` drops isError; a failed fetch renders the empty submissions state (count 0) with no error indicator or retry.

Consistent pattern across all three mediation-workspace read panels. The parent MediationWorkspacePage.tsx only guards the top-level useDispute fetch (isError branch at line 204 with a retry button); the per-tab sub-queries above have no equivalent, so a sub-query failure on the Chat/Timeline/Submissions tab silently masquerades as empty data. Mutations in the same files are handled correctly (try/catch -> onToastError), and sibling MoveFolderDialog.tsx:296 already models the right shape (`{ data, isLoading, error }` with an explicit error branch at line 427). Fix: surface isError with an inline error + refetch, mirroring MoveFolderDialog / the parent page.
Static-analysis only (no compile/run). Severity medium: user-facing correctness/UX defect on the mediation hot path, graceful (no crash) but hides load failures with no recovery.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/pages/CreateDisputePage.tsx:29-42 — handleSubmit() collects the full dispute form (respondentId/category/subject/description) but never calls any create-dispute API: the try block is just `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))` (line 35) then `navigate('/disputes')` (line 36). The form data is silently discarded; the user sees a 1s spinner and a redirect that looks like success. This is an abandoned first-cut stub of the real FileDisputePage.

It is an orphan: the /disputes/new route is wired to FileDisputePageRoute (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/disputes.tsx:482), NOT CreateDisputePage. But CreateDisputePage is still exported from the public barrel (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/pages/index.ts:6 and features/disputes/index.ts), so it remains importable/discoverable and would silently drop data if ever mounted.

Secondary: CreateDisputePage.tsx uses hardcoded English JSX strings with no i18n — 'Back to Disputes' (line 50), 'File New Dispute' (line 52), the intro paragraph (line 53-55), the error string 'Failed to create dispute. Please try again.' (line 38), 'Respondent ID' (line 67), 'Enter the ID of the other party' (line 77) — inconsistent with the fully-i18n'd sibling MediationWorkspacePage/FileDisputePage.

Same recognized pattern as the already-landed backlog item code-review-mobile-rn-report-fault-fake-submit (RN report-fault fake submit). Fix: delete CreateDisputePage (dead duplicate) and drop its barrel export, or wire it to the real useFileDispute mutation + i18n if it is meant to be the canonical page.

Static-analysis only (no compile/run). Severity medium: dead-code/completeness defect that discards user input if the orphan is ever mounted; currently not reachable via routing, hence confidence medium not high.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/journal/page.tsx:113-116 — `handleSubscribe(e)` calls `e.preventDefault()` then `if (email.trim()) setSubscribed(true)` and returns. There is NO fetch / API mutation: the entered email is never sent anywhere, it is simply discarded when the component unmounts.

The UI nonetheless renders a localized success confirmation: line 217-218 `{subscribed ?

{t('newsletterSuccess')}

:
...}` — a public visitor who submits the Journal newsletter form is told (via `pages.journal.newsletterSuccess`) they subscribed, but no subscription was recorded server-side. Grep confirms the file contains no `fetch`/`api`/`subscribe` network call (only i18n keys named *newsletter*).

Distinct from the prior 2026-08-12 fake-submit findings (sell/page.tsx, report/page.tsx, realtor/[id] contact form) — this is the /[locale]/journal route. User-facing data-loss-of-intent on a public SEO page. Fix: POST the email to the reality-server newsletter/subscription endpoint (or a Next route) inside handleSubscribe, gate `setSubscribed(true)` on a 2xx, and surface a localized error state on failure.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/inquiries/page.tsx:47-50 — `handleCancel` calls `cancelInquiry.mutate(inquiry.id)` (fire-and-forget) and immediately `setShowCancelConfirm(false)`. `cancelInquiry = useCancelInquiry()` (line 41) is a TanStack useMutation, but line 48 is the ONLY reference to the mutation object in the whole file: no `onError`, no `cancelInquiry.isError`/`.error` branch, no `mutateAsync` + try/catch, no pending guard.

Effect: on a failed cancel (network error, 4xx/5xx, race with an already-responded inquiry) the confirmation dialog closes and the card still shows the inquiry as active with the Cancel button — the user believes the inquiry was cancelled when it was not, and gets zero feedback. The `.error-state` block at line 329-334 handles ONLY the page-load `useMyInquiries` query error, not the mutation.

Matches the SKILL Frontend pattern 'useMutation call with no error handling (no isError branch, no onError, no ErrorBoundary above)'. Distinct from prior reality-web passes (none touched inquiries/page.tsx). Fix: surface `cancelInquiry.isError` (localized toast/inline error), keep the confirm open or restore it on failure, and disable the confirm button while `cancelInquiry.isPending`. (Secondary: this whole route is hardcoded English — 0 useTranslations — but that folds into the known reality-web i18n backlog, not this finding.)

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/price-map/page.tsx:37 — `v == null ? '—' : `${Math.round(v).toLocaleString('sk-SK')} €`` and line 96 `value: totalListings.toLocaleString('sk-SK')` pin the number-format locale to Slovak even though the page is fully next-intl localized (line 40 `const t = useTranslations('pages.priceMap')`).

Effect on the sk/cs/de/en portal: a German (/de/…) or English (/en/…) visitor sees Slovak-grouped numbers (narrow-no-break-space thousands separator, e.g. `1 234 €`) instead of their locale's convention (`1.234 €` / `1,234 €`). This is a distinct axis from the existing reality-web i18n findings, which are about untranslated STRINGS — here the strings are translated but the numeric/currency FORMAT ignores the active locale.

The same hardcoded-locale smell also appears in realtor/[id]/page.tsx:311 (`toLocaleString('sk-SK')`) and realtor/listings/page.tsx:17 (`Intl.NumberFormat('en', …)`), so a shared `formatPrice(value, currency, locale)` helper keyed off the route `[locale]` param / `useLocale()` would fix all three. Landable low-severity cleanup; no crash.
